name: Autosomal Dominant Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple punctate hyperkeratotic papules on the palms and soles
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis with focal parakeratosis and acanthosis
Exclusion of other palmoplantar keratoderma subtypes by clinical and genetic evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic punctate palmoplantar keratoderma lesions with a positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may identify mutations in AAGAB or other associated genes but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis with focal parakeratosis and acanthosis
Negative fungal cultures to exclude tinea
genetic: Mutations in AAGAB gene associated with autosomal dominant punctate palmoplantar keratoderma
Other gene mutations reported include COL14A1 and others in rare cases
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Clinical exclusion of other keratoderma subtypes

distinguishingFeatures: Larger keratotic lesions with central keratin plug
Later onset and different lesion distribution
Linear hyperkeratosis along fingers and palms
Different inheritance pattern and gene mutations (e.g., DSG1)
Mutations in KRT9 or KRT1 genes

redFlags: Rapid progression of lesions with ulceration or bleeding
Development of painful fissures impairing hand or foot function
Signs of secondary infection such as purulence or cellulitis
